clue.text: Cracking up-the grin sat oddly

indicators.note: the letters of these three words are arranged oddly, so they are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is losing composure, a strange grin sitting on their face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' shuffles the ten letters of THE GRIN SAT. 'Cracking up' looks like laughter but means breaking into pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe something breaking apart into fragments, or a person collapsing under strain.

clue.text: Bear up and ring

indicators.note: in a down clue, up tells us to read the bear's name from bottom to top

parts.note: Pooh is the famous bear of children's stories, Winnie-the-Pooh

explanation.surface: An instruction to put up with something and telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns POOH round in this down entry. 'Bear' looks like a verb (endure) but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoop is a circular band, the same shape as a ring.

clue.text: A flier takes part, showing some delicacy

parts.note: a tit is a small bird, something that flies
a bit is a part or piece of something

explanation.surface: A bird pecks off a piece, showing it has some refined manners.
explanation.definitionFit: A tasty morsel of food is a choice treat, a small delicacy.

clue.text: Claire's made fancy cakes

indicators.note: made fancy suggests the letters are dressed up into a new arrangement

parts.note: the woman's name with its possessive S, all seven letters used

explanation.surface: Claire has baked some elaborate cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges CLAIRES; here the S of the possessive counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclairs are long choux-pastry cakes filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: The flag of the rainbow goddess

definitions.meaning: flag is a name for the wild yellow ... plant
in Greek myth ... is the messenger goddess of the rainbow

explanation.surface: A banner belonging to the deity of the rainbow.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant called flag belongs to this genus, and the Greek goddess personifying the rainbow bears this name.

clue.text: No particular military man

explanation.definitionFit: The word means broad rather than specific, and is also a high army rank.

clue.text: A number to impress a woman? Quite!

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
to get someone is to affect or impress them
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a song might win a lady over, and gets emphatic agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' suggests a song, but A is itself and the number is the Roman 50.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether means completely or entirely, as the exclamation 'Quite!' agrees totally.

clue.text: Dire photos misrepresent men of the cloth

indicators.note: to misrepresent is to present wrongly, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Terrible pictures give a false impression of the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misrepresent' rearranges the ten letters of DIRE PHOTOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Men of the cloth are clergymen, collectively the clergy or the priestly body.

clue.text: A slight lack of clarity in speech

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an insulting remark and also indistinct, run-together speech.

clue.text: He would ride after the Italian beast

parts.note: post is the Latin-derived prefix meaning after
il is the Italian word for the
a lion is a wild beast

explanation.surface: A rider follows behind some Italian animal.
explanation.walkthrough: A postillion rode the leading horse of a carriage team.
explanation.definitionFit: A postillion is a rider mounted on one of the horses drawing a coach.

clue.text: Call for more directions to the centre

parts.note: E and N are the compass points east and north
the core is the centre of something

explanation.surface: Someone asks for directions to the middle of town.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience's shout asking a performer to repeat or continue the performance.

clue.text: Barrow boys-they have to work out the prices

definitions.text: they have to work out the prices
definitions.meaning: read whimsically as people who cost things

explanation.definitionFit: Costers, short for costermongers, are British street sellers of fruit and vegetables from barrows; read literally, costers are people who cost goods.

clue.text: The transferring of property or a vehicle

definitions.meaning: the legal process of moving ownership of land or a house

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the legal transfer of land ownership and any means of transport.

clue.text: Starting displaying

definitions.meaning: showing something off to advantage, as a frame enhances a picture

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means beginning a journey, and also enhancing or showing something to advantage.

clue.text: Fume if set at odds before midday

indicators.note: before midday describes the morning, which is abbreviated
things at odds are out of line, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for the hours before midday

explanation.surface: Someone may get angry if a setting is wrong in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Fume and the other word both mean vapour, and both mean to seethe with anger.

clue.text: Down-payment made for listening equipment by a home

parts.note: the ear is the body's hearing organ
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: A deposit is paid on a hearing aid at a care home.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest money is a deposit paid as a pledge to secure a deal.

clue.text: Note overdue transport

parts.note: E is a musical note
late means overdue

explanation.surface: A memo about a delayed bus or train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' looks like a noun for buses but is the verb meaning to fill with delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport someone is to carry them away with joy, to thrill them.

clue.text: School-head requiring high hedge

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: tall means high

explanation.surface: A headteacher demands a tall hedge around the school grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hedge' looks like a garden plant but is the verb meaning to evade.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall is to play for time and avoid committing, as one hedges.

clue.text: A minute mark

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a brief written memo and also to pay attention or observe.

clue.text: A man's article none read

parts.note: the is the definite article
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A man has a piece of writing that nobody has read.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, short for Theodore.

clue.text: Give attention to cooking meat for buffet

definitions.meaning: to spoon fat over a roasting joint

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to moisten a roast with its juices, and also to beat or thrash.

clue.text: Scholar taking a knife to settle accounts

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
a lance is a surgical knife

explanation.surface: An academic uses a knife to resolve a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: To balance the books is to make the accounts add up.

clue.text: Print a letter with serious results

parts.note: en is the spelt-out name of the letter N
grave means serious

explanation.surface: Someone writes a letter that has dire consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave is to cut a design into a plate from which images are printed.

clue.text: Edge back around a Greek character making a witty remark

indicators.note: around says the reversed edge goes round the Greek letter
back says the word for edge is to be read in reverse

parts.note: marge is an old word for margin or edge
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person sidles round an edge while making a clever quip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the old word for edge, giving EGRAM, and 'around' wraps it about the Greek letter; 'character' suggests a person but is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short, pointed and clever saying.

clue.text: Followed without the right, that's for certain

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for followed sits round the letter

parts.note: ensued means followed or came after
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone followed without having the right to do so, and that is certain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made sure or guaranteed is secured as a certainty.

clue.text: Rushes about and puts people in their place

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone hurries around putting people firmly in their place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts people in their place' sounds like scolding but means showing them to their seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Ushers show people to their seats at a theatre, wedding or church.

clue.text: Animal having a defective organ

indicators.note: something defective is faulty, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A creature has a faulty internal organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defective' rearranges ORGAN into ANGOR, and the clue's 'a' goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An Angora is a breed of goat, rabbit or cat with long silky hair.

clue.text: Hands back for exchange

indicators.note: back says the word for hands is read in reverse

parts.note: paws are informal for hands

explanation.surface: Someone gives the cards back in a trade.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade one thing for another is to swap.

clue.text: Not all but most unhappily cause shock

indicators.note: not all of the words are used, only a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Everyone is shocked, though most only mildly unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to daze or shock someone.

clue.text: Businessmen who are innovative like reflective fellows

parts.note: something innovative is new

indicators.note: reflective, as in a mirror, means the word is reversed

parts.note: as means like
gents are men, fellows

explanation.surface: Entrepreneurs are inventive in the way thoughtful men are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflective' turns AS into SA. 'reflective' seems to mean thoughtful but signals a mirror image.
explanation.definitionFit: Newsagents are shopkeepers selling papers and magazines, so traders or businessmen.

clue.text: A coffee-bar in Jamaica features the local produce

indicators.note: in says the answer lies inside the following words

explanation.surface: A coffee shop in Jamaica serves the coffee grown on the island.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'jamaiCA FEatures'; 'the local produce' completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafe is a small restaurant serving coffee and light meals.

clue.text: Putting thoughts into words is no longer crucial

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
pressing means urgent, crucial

explanation.surface: Saying what one thinks is no longer vital.
explanation.definitionFit: Expressing ideas means stating or voicing them.
